title: Arjuna sees his own people across the field

verses.sa: संजय उवाचएवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: Spoken to thus by Gudakesha, Hrishikesha stationed the finest chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings.
verses.angle: Hrishikesha places the chariot between the armies
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: The battlefield is set. Krishna has driven the chariot right into the space between the two armies. Listen to where he stops.

body.text: Sanjaya says: Spoken to thus by Gudakesha, Hrishikesha stationed the finest chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings. The verse names Hrishikesha, the lord of the senses, and Gudakesha, the conqueror of sleep. He places the finest chariot in the middle of both armies, right in front of the elders and the kings. Krishna tells Arjuna to look at the assembled Kurus gathered there.

verses.sa: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् । उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥
verses.tr: Standing before Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers, Krishna said, "O Partha, behold these assembled Kurus."
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for one word Krishna uses to stop Arjuna's eyes on the front line, before the arrows fly.

body.text: Standing before Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers, Krishna said, "O Partha, behold these assembled Kurus." Krishna says, pashya, behold. He does not say fight, or attack, or strike. He says only behold. He wants Arjuna to look, to see the faces, before he acts. Krishna speaks to Arjuna in front of the kings, telling him to behold the assembled Kurus.

verses.tr: Then Arjuna, son of Pritha, saw fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, fathers-in-law, and well-wishers standing there.
verses.angle: Partha sees a long list of relations standing there
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Krishna has pointed the way, and now Arjuna looks. What he sees on the battlefield turns a war into a family tragedy.

body.text: Then Arjuna, son of Pritha, saw fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, fathers-in-law, and well-wishers standing there. Arjuna, son of Pritha, looks and sees a long string of relations, fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, and grandsons, all standing there. Seeing all these relatives standing there, Arjuna sinks into grief and speaks in fear.

verses.sa: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि । तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥
verses.tr: Seeing all his relatives standing there, Arjuna sank into grief and spoke in fear.
verses.angle: Kunteya sees his kin on both sides
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya carries the scene forward by telling us what Arjuna sees when he looks past the ranks.

body.text: Seeing all his relatives standing there, Arjuna sank into grief and spoke in fear. Arjuna looks across both armies and sees fathers-in-law, friends, and relatives on every side. He does not see enemies, but his own people standing ready for battle. Arjuna turns to Krishna and speaks of the pity and grief that overwhelm him.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: Seeing my own people gathered here, eager for battle, I am overcome with pity and grief, O Krishna.
verses.angle: Arjuna names pity and grief to Krishna
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has already recognized the faces on both sides. Now he names the feeling to Krishna. Listen to how he speaks.

body.text: Arjuna says: Seeing my own people gathered here, eager for battle, I am overcome with pity and grief, O Krishna. Arjuna names the feeling directly to Krishna: I am overcome by supreme pity, and I am grieving. He does not hide it. He tells Krishna, having seen these my own people assembled before me. He then describes the physical collapse that pity causes in his own body.

verses.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
verses.tr: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end.
verses.angle: The body gives out in order
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stands on the battlefield, looking at his own kin. His body begins to break down before his mind can fully catch up.

body.text: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end. Each word here is a part of the body giving out in order. First the limbs, then the mouth, then the whole body shakes, and finally the hair stands on end. The collapse is physical before it is mental. Then he speaks of the bow slipping from his hand and the skin burning, as the collapse becomes total.

verses.sa: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
verses.tr: My bow slips from my hand. My skin burns. I cannot stand steady, and my mind reels.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has always been the greatest warrior. Listen for the first sign that his strength is failing.

body.text: My bow slips from my hand. My skin burns. I cannot stand steady, and my mind reels. Listen for the word Gandiva, his famous bow, and how it slips from his hand. The weapon falls because his mind has already surrendered. He then names the physical signs of his collapse, skin burning and mind spinning.

verses.sa: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव । न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥
verses.tr: O Keshava, I see only inauspicious signs, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just told Krishna his body is failing him. Now he tells Krishna what he sees around him. Listen for the signs he notices and the reason he gives for not fighting.

body.text: O Keshava, I see only inauspicious signs, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle. Arjuna says he sees viparitanani, opposite or inauspicious signs. He says he sees no shreyah, no real good, in killing his own people in this battle. Arjuna then tells Krishna he does not want victory, kingdom, or even life itself.

verses.sa: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च । किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
verses.tr: I do not desire victory, Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are pleasures or even life?
verses.angle: Govinda and the cost of victory
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Carrying on from his refusal to fight, Arjuna now rejects the very goals of the war. Listen to how he dismisses them.

body.text: I do not desire victory, Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are pleasures or even life? Listen to the word Govinda, and the phrase what use is kingdom to us. Arjuna rejects these goals because the people he must defeat to get them are his own. He then turns to the men standing before him, the very ones for whom he once desired this kingdom.

verses.sa: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च । त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
verses.tr: Those for whom we wanted kingdom, pleasures, and comfort stand here in battle, ready to give up life and wealth.
verses.angle: Kingdom desired for the very people giving up their lives
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna looks at the enemy lines and asks who the war is actually for. Listen to the people standing there.

body.text: Those for whom we wanted kingdom, pleasures, and comfort stand here in battle, ready to give up life and wealth. The people he wanted the kingdom for are the same ones standing on the battlefield, ready to give up their lives and wealth. That is what breaks him. He now looks closer at the faces of those relatives, teachers, and elders standing in the two armies.

verses.sa: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः । मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥
verses.tr: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna looks across the battlefield at the faces he knows and lists them one by one.

body.text: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives. He names them one by one, teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, and in-laws, until the battlefield becomes a family gathering he cannot bear to attack. He says he will not kill them even if they kill him, let alone for a kingdom.

verses.sa: एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन । अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
verses.tr: I do not want to kill these people, even if they kill me, O Madhusudana. Not even for the rule of the three worlds, much less for the earth.
verses.angle: ghnato'pi, even if they kill me
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stops his bow at the sight of his kin and asks what good a kingdom would do if it cost them their lives. Listen to how he weighs his life against the whole world.

body.text: I do not want to kill these people, even if they kill me, O Madhusudana. Not even for the rule of the three worlds, much less for the earth. Listen to one phrase, ghnato'pi, even if they kill me. Arjuna is not just afraid; he is saying his life has no price, and he will not trade it for rule over the three worlds. He then asks Krishna what joy they could possibly find in killing the sons of Dhritarashtra.

verses.sa: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन । पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥
verses.tr: O Janardana, what joy would come to us by killing these sons of Dhritarashtra? Killing these aggressors would only bring us sin.
verses.angle: Arjuna counts the cost of killing his own kin
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just listed his kin and teachers on the battlefield. He names the enemy, but his heart is not in it. Listen for the cost he counts.

body.text: O Janardana, what joy would come to us by killing these sons of Dhritarashtra? Killing these aggressors would only bring us sin. Arjuna calls them aggressors, yet he says killing them will bring no joy and only stain the killers with sin. He asks again, how can we be happy after killing our own blood, O Madhava?

verses.sa: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् । स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava?
verses.angle: swajanam and sukhinah: kinship and happiness
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna now draws the final line, refusing to trade the happiness of kin for the grief of war. Listen for the word that seals his refusal.

body.text: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava? The word here is swajanam, our own people. Arjuna says that if he kills his own people, he cannot be happy. He does not say he might be sad, he says happiness is impossible, and that is why he refuses to fight. Yet even as he refuses, Arjuna sees that his opponents do not see the wrong in destroying a family.
